plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down - bidding exactly my value of $39 maximizes my expected profit. If I win, I pay less than $39, ensuring positive profit; if I overbid, I risk winning at a loss, and if I underbid, I risk losing profitable opportunities.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing a profitable auction. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot game, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. With a low value of $1, I should bid exactly $1 to ensure I never overpay - if I win, I'll pay less than $1, and if I lose, I avoid overpaying for an item worth little to me. This truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.
